name: ShadowLab training scenarios
warning: ShadowLab is intentionally vulnerable. It binds to loopback only, contains synthetic data only, and must never be exposed to a network or deployed to production.

scenarios.title: Cleartext HTTP transport
scenarios.summary: A checkout page served over cleartext HTTP with no HSTS, so the whole flow is readable on the wire.
scenarios.demo: Open /lab/transport/checkout and observe the http:// origin and the absent Strict-Transport-Security header.

scenarios.title: Security headers missing
scenarios.summary: A page rendered without CSP, X-Content-Type-Options or X-Frame-Options.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/headers/console and inspect the response headers.
scenarios.description: A JSON API response is served with no X-Content-Type-Options and no Content-Security-Policy, so a browser is free to sniff the body and the page has no script origin policy.

scenarios.title: Session cookie without security attributes
scenarios.summary: A session cookie issued without HttpOnly, Secure or SameSite, so it is readable by script and sent on cross-site requests.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/cookies/session and inspect the Set-Cookie header.
scenarios.safe: The cookie value is a synthetic placeholder.

scenarios.title: Verbose error messages
scenarios.summary: A failing request returns a stack trace with internal file paths and the query that broke.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/errors/checkout and read the JSON error body.
scenarios.safe: The traceback is a fixed synthetic string, not a real exception.

scenarios.title: Insecure CORS configuration
scenarios.summary: A profile endpoint answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/cors/profile and inspect the Access-Control-* headers.

scenarios.title: Reflected input rendered unencoded
scenarios.summary: A search page echoes the name parameter into HTML without encoding it.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/xss/echo?name=<script>alert(1)</script> and observe the unencoded reflection in the body.
scenarios.safe: The payload is reflected as text; ShadowLab never executes it and the page has no other script.

scenarios.title: SQL injection (error-based simulation)
scenarios.summary: A product lookup passes the id parameter into a query and returns the database error verbatim.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/sqli/product?id=1' and observe the SQL error text in the response.
scenarios.safe: No database is queried; the error text is a fixed synthetic string and no data is read or written.

scenarios.title: Path traversal (synthetic filesystem)
scenarios.summary: A download endpoint accepts a file path parameter and returns a synthetic file from a fake filesystem.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/files/download?file=../../../../etc/passwd and observe the passwd-shaped content.
scenarios.safe: The content is a hard-coded sample held in memory; no host file is opened and every traversal attempt is answered from the same synthetic table.

scenarios.title: Insecure direct object reference
scenarios.summary: Account records are addressed by a sequential id and returned without authentication; 1002 and 1003 belong to other synthetic customers.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/idor/account/1001, then 1002 and 1003, and compare the returned owners.

scenarios.title: Authentication and authorization logic flaws
scenarios.summary: An administrative panel is served without any authentication, and the login form posts over cleartext with a synthetic account list.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/auth/admin-panel and observe that no credentials were required.
scenarios.safe: The panel shows synthetic users only; there is no session and no credential store.

scenarios.title: Unsafe file-upload validation
scenarios.summary: An upload form accepts any extension and does not validate content type. ShadowLab refuses the POST itself, so nothing is ever stored or executed.
scenarios.demo: Open /lab/upload to see the form, then note that every POST is answered with 405 by design.
scenarios.safe: Uploads are never accepted, written to disk or executed; the demo ends at the form.

scenarios.title: Open redirect
scenarios.summary: A continue parameter is used as the redirect target. ShadowLab only redirects to local paths and refuses absolute URLs, which keeps the demo contained.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/redirect?next=/lab/landing and observe the 302 to the supplied path.
scenarios.safe: Only same-site targets are honoured; an absolute URL is refused with 400.
scenarios.containment_note: The lab only honours same-site targets and answers an absolute URL with 400, so the off-site redirect that ST-022 detects cannot be produced here by design.

scenarios.title: Exposed debug and diagnostic routes
scenarios.summary: Diagnostic routes publish a synthetic environment, build metadata and a feature-flag dump to anyone.
scenarios.safe: Every value is a synthetic placeholder; no real environment variable is read.

scenarios.title: Insecure API access control
scenarios.summary: An export endpoint returns API keys for every synthetic tenant without checking who is asking.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/api-keys/export and observe the key material.

scenarios.title: Weak input validation
scenarios.summary: A quantity parameter accepts negative numbers, quotes and markup, and reflects the raw value back into the page.
scenarios.demo: Fetch /lab/input/quantity?q=-1 with markup and observe the unvalidated echo.
